correctness.rationale: For a fixed spot order, when car sigma_j arrives, the smaller-labeled cars occupy exactly their designated spots; the allowed preferences for sigma_j run from one past the nearest larger label on its left up to j. This proves the fiber product by induction over arrivals. For a rise a<b at i,i+1, the two old distances A,B satisfy A+1<=B<=i+1 and the two new distances are B-1,1. A later nearest larger predecessor changes only for a value strictly between a and b with no larger entry in the intervening suffix; then its distance increases from j-i-1 to j-i. Thus the local factor is between 1/(i+1) and i/(i+1), and the later factors lie between 1 and their full telescoping product n-i. The increasing order and the stated (2,...,i,1,n,i+1,...,n-1) order realize the respective extremes, including empty prefix or suffix. For the global maximum, t+(n+1)/t-2 sqrt(n+1)=(t-sqrt(n+1))^2/t gives the rounding error; the endpoint and small-n inequalities follow from the exact envelopes. Independent raw preference enumeration through n=5 confirmed both extrema at each position, checking 1, 6, 36 and 240 rising swaps respectively.
residual_risks: The independent replay is a small-n cross-check only; the exact case analysis supplies the proof for all n. No claim is made for swaps of nonadjacent positions or changed parking rules.

value.rationale: Knowing the increasing outcome is the most likely does not tell whether a single new inversion makes a nearby outcome less likely. The exact positionwise envelope gives the first size allowing an increase, distinguishes the last position from all earlier positions for n>=4, and shows a single local move can amplify mass by order n at positions of order sqrt(n). These are quantitative features of the classical permutation law not supplied by its global mode or an isolated example.
residual_risks: The result concerns only one rising adjacent swap; it does not order aggregate inversion statistics or characterize general move sequences.
